eic.19/count/summary.instrument: Composite = mean of category mean-ranks over the categories at least one method at this address fully covers. A method missing any of them is incomplete, not last: the composite cell is a dash and it drops out of the headline ranking while still ranking inside every category it covers. Lower is better. Avocado.classes: Position-transductive: its genomic factors are per-position free parameters, so a chromosome it never fitted returns its random initialisation rather than a degraded prediction. Avocado.training: Retraining under both live regimes, eic.19 and eic.pilot, with the uniform rule of §5: every trainable method selects its best checkpoint on V_, by the same rule, and B_ is never read during training. The joint fit moves off chr20, which is now an eval chromosome: under eic.19 it fits chr19, and under eic.pilot it returns to the ENCODE Pilot Regions, which is what the paper does. Genomic factors are then fit per chromosome — three per regime, on chr20, chr21 and chr22 only, because §4 blanks Avocado's genome-wide cell and a blanked cell is not computed. The spread device is refit under §7: sigma comes from training-set residuals only, never from V_ and never from B_. Every sigma fit on V_ eval pairs is void under Rule 1.
Avocado.what: Tensor factorisation over (cell, assay, position): one MLP on concatenated cell, assay, and per-position genomic factors (Schreiber, Bilmes & Noble 2020). Max’s PyTorch port, vendored byte-identical, retrained by us. Cannot predict a position it never fitted.

caveats: Quote count CRPS with its oracle-scaled / scale-error split and the 0.09 floor.
Version-over-version arrows use the 0.1195 seed-alone bar, which is never a cross-method floor.
B_ is predicted exactly once, from the checkpoint selected on V_. Re-scoring those stored predictions is free; re-predicting is not.

Six rows are stamped: the challenge-truth B_ held-out cell on each board, and the store-truth V_breadth cells on each board at both scopes, held-out and genome-wide. The rest wait on score passes still running — store truth on both B_ panels, and the V_matched panel under both regimes.
CANDI.classes: One CANDI row per regime — the current best. Version history is a separate figure, never extra rows: the ranker ranks across methods within a cell, so an extra CANDI version would shift every rival's rank. Under eic.19 CANDI is in-sample on 1 of 23 chromosomes, and that fraction is printed on every genome-wide cell. CANDI conditions on covariates, not a per-cell embedding; the board still measures missing-mark transfer within a cell type it has seen. Badges are read off the stamped rows, not declared here. Nothing is ranked until the seed noise floor (t86) is measured.
CANDI.scoring: Internal bench (python -m candi.bench), not the external rival scorer. That path emits a native Negative Binomial on counts, a native Gaussian on p-values and a native peak probability, so CANDI uses no spread device. Covariate-sensitivity numbers can only come from this internal path.
CANDI.training: Retraining under both live regimes, eic.19 and eic.pilot, with the uniform rule of §5: every trainable method selects its best checkpoint on V_, by the same rule, and B_ is never read during training. Both regimes train the same model with heads count+signal+peak. eic.19 fits chr19 only; eic.pilot fits the 44 hg38 ENCODE Pilot Regions minus their overlap with chr20/21/22. Training stops on a stalled V_ (--early-stop-epochs, default 3, counted in epochs) rather than at a fixed epoch count: the number of epochs is read off the curve, not set in advance. Both stamped B_ panels, eic.19 and eic.pilot, were predicted on CPU nodes, one shard per chromosome, from the checkpoint that rule selected on V_.
CANDI.what: The CANDI model: grouped Conv1D plus a DNA tower plus a RoPE transformer, then a grouped decoder with FiLM and a depth-offset negative-binomial count head. The queued runs also train a Gaussian signal head and a Bernoulli peak head. CANDI is stamped on both boards, eic.19 and eic.pilot: the challenge-truth B_ held-out row on each, and the store-truth V_breadth rows on each at both scopes, held-out and genome-wide. Its store-truth B_ and V_matched cells are still pending on both boards.

count/crps.estimator_notes: Default: closed-form CRPS = E|X − y| − ½ E|X − X′| (metrics.py::nb_crps), p = n / (n + μ) clipped to [10⁻⁹, 1 − 10⁻⁹], y ← max(y, 0). For n ≤ 10⁴: Pfaff-transformed ₂F₁ Gini term; result clamped max(·, 0). For n > 10⁴: Poisson-limit branch with sd ratio r = √(1 + μ/n). Track mean then macro mean. Opt-in --crps-approx K: fair sampled CRPS (nb_crps_sampled), k = K (full-genome baselines planned k=100, seed 0), gamma–Poisson draws, Ferro 2008 denominator k(k−1), no clamp at 0. Provenance then carries crps_estimator=fair_sampled, crps_k, crps_seed. Stamped chromosome-21 baselines: closed form at producer floor n=10⁴, not the pre-registered 10⁶. Computed from metrics.py::nb_crps and distributional.py::nb_suite.
count/crps.question: If each bin is a negative-binomial forecast of raw counts, how far is that whole distribution from the held-out count?
count/crps.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; floor ±0.09 (frozen pre-CANDII target-clustered; not a full-genome cross-method remeasure). Always quote crps_oracle_scaled and scale_error. If sampled, also quote k and seed. CANDI self-arrows use the 0.1195 seed-alone bar, not this floor. Count and p-value CRPS never share a column.

count/crps_oracle_scaled.estimator_notes: c* = arg min_c CRPS(NB(n, μ · 2^c), y) on grid c ∈ [−6, 6] step 0.25 then refine ±0.25 at 0.01 (distributional.py::oracle_scale). Grid search may subsample fit_budget=20,000 positions (seed=0); reported CRPS is on the full track at chosen c*. Dispersion n is not rescaled for this key. Same estimator as crps (closed form or sampled with shared seed). In-sample oracle: scale_error may be slightly negative. Computed from distributional.py::oracle_scale / nb_suite.
count/crps_oracle_scaled.question: After giving the forecast a free per-assay multiplicative rescale of the mean, how good is the distribution (capability)?
count/crps_oracle_scaled.read_rules: Lower is better; companion. Never quote without raw crps and scale_error. Not a cross-method rank column by itself.

count/nb_nll.estimator_notes: Training twin (distributional.py::nb_nll): p = n / (n + μ), probs = clip(1 − p, [10⁻⁶, 1 − 10⁻⁶]), total = max(n, 10⁻⁶), k = max(counts, 0), NLL = −mean[total log(1 − probs) + k log(probs) − log Γ(total + k) + log Γ(1 + k) + log Γ(total)]. Mean over all eval bins of the track (the imp population, not a training mask). Computed from distributional.py::nb_nll / harness.py::loss_block.
count/nb_nll.question: What mean per-bin negative-binomial NLL does the count head assign to held-out raw counts?
count/nb_nll.read_rules: Lower is better; per_family; never in the composite; never ranked against Gaussian NLL. Sampled CRPS does not change NLL. Count-space NLL and p-value-space NLL never share a table.

count/scale_error.estimator_notes: scale_error = crps − crps_oracle_scaled (distributional.py::nb_suite). Same estimator on both terms (common random numbers if sampled).
count/scale_error.question: How much of the count CRPS would one per-assay mean rescale remove?
count/scale_error.read_rules: Lower is better (can be slightly negative); companion. Quote the triple or none.

diagnostics/biokeep.estimator_notes: Mean silhouette over bio_label (region) (covariate.py::biokeep). Board headline from depthblind_biokeep.bio_silhouette (flatten_c_block).
diagnostics/biokeep.question: Did the latent stay invariant because it still separates regions, or because it collapsed?
diagnostics/biokeep.read_rules: Higher is better; companion of depthblind; never render depth-blind without this; CANDI-only.

diagnostics/covshare.estimator_notes: Shapley effects on V(S) = Var(E[f | X_S]) with inner-sample bias correction, both variances ddof=1, n_outer=64, n_inner=8, seed 0, f = level (covariate.py::covshare). Four covariates → 16 subsets exact. Shares sum to 1 when total > 10⁻¹². Board scalar: none (per-covariate dict omitted by flatten).
diagnostics/covshare.question: Of the variance in predicted level, what share does each covariate own (Shapley, not Sobol)?
diagnostics/covshare.read_rules: No direction on the registry; no board number today; CANDI-only. Never invent for rivals.

diagnostics/covspec.estimator_notes: Aspects = level, shape, dispersion, tail (aspects_of). Matrix entry = mean |Δaspect| / std(base aspect) under marginal resample. Per aspect, gap = (m_1 − m_2) / m_1. Board headline = mean_gap (covariate.py::covspec). Construction is local (EVAL_PLAN D11), not a standard MIG of latents.
diagnostics/covspec.question: When each covariate is scrambled, does each aspect of the NB profile move mainly under one covariate?
diagnostics/covspec.read_rules: Higher is better; diagnostic; CANDI-only; not in the composite.

diagnostics/covuse.estimator_notes: Per covariate k, L_obs = mean CRPS_NB(predict(cov)). For R = 200 resamples (default, seed 0): marginal and conditional nulls; p = (1 + #{L_r ≤ L_obs}) / (R + 1); uses_covariate = 1[p_marginal < 0.05]. within_batch_d_crps must be exactly 0 (covariate.py::covuse). Board scalar: flatten_c_block has no headline for nested covuse — omitted unless already a finite scalar. Computed from covariate.py::covuse.
diagnostics/covuse.question: Does scrambling one told covariate make the count-head CRPS worse than the true prompt?
diagnostics/covuse.read_rules: Registry direction is higher, but no panel aggregate is defined in code. CANDI-lineage only; empty for every stamped row; never invent for rivals.

diagnostics/depthblind.estimator_notes: depthblind returns kBET rejection rate (k=20, α=0.05, n_test=200, seed 0), iLISI (k capped), batch_asw = mean(1 − |s|), plus biokeep fields (covariate.py::depthblind). Board: flatten_c_block omits depthblind — no single headline. Site cannot show a number until a headline is chosen. Computed from covariate.py::depthblind / kBET.
diagnostics/depthblind.question: Is the encoder latent invariant to input depth (DSF batch), by kBET / iLISI / batch ASW?
diagnostics/depthblind.read_rules: Higher better on the registry, but no scalar is extracted. Never quote without biokeep (D13). CANDI-only.

diagnostics/depthcounterfact.estimator_notes: One foreground: top 2% (min 5) of the deepest truth, jitter seed 0, optional truth ≥ 1 purity (covariate.py::depthcounterfact). For each true DSF level, argmin CRPS over told depths. Board headline = frac_min_at_true. constant_answer_value = 1 / n_levels (0.25 on a four-level ladder).
diagnostics/depthcounterfact.question: Told a false depth, does the count forecast whose told depth matches the real downsampled track win?
diagnostics/depthcounterfact.read_rules: Higher is better; quote with the 0.25 floor and no 0.73 ceiling. 0.25 is “always answer full depth”, not chance. CANDI-only.

diagnostics/depthdir.estimator_notes: Ladder offsets (0, −1, −2, −3) log2 (covariate.py::depthdir). monotone_frac = mean(Δlevel ≤ 0) over adjacent steps × units. Headline on the board = monotone_frac.
diagnostics/depthdir.question: As told depth is stepped down the DSF ladder, does predicted level fall at every step?
diagnostics/depthdir.read_rules: Higher is better; diagnostic; CANDI-only; not in the composite. Never invent for rivals.

pval/auprc.estimator_notes: Step-wise average precision, ties collapsed to one threshold (binary.py::average_precision): AP = Σ_k (R_k − R_{k−1}) P_k, with P_k = TP / (TP + FP) and R_k = TP / TP_end. Scores sorted descending (mergesort); equal scores share one threshold (last-of-tie). No positives → NaN. Score vector = peak_score if a peak head exists, else predicted p-value (or count mean). Computed from binary.py::average_precision / binary_suite.
pval/auprc.question: Ranking bins by the method’s peak score (or, if none, by predicted signal), how well are MACS2 peak bins placed above background?
pval/auprc.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; always quote peak_base_rate. AUROC is not on the board. A point-only rival’s AUPRC is a coverage ranking, not a peak classifier: eDICE, Avocado, and ChromImpute do not output a peak probability, so the scorer ranks each bin by predicted signal against MACS2 labels. CANDI's peak head, when its rows land, emits a per-bin Bernoulli probability and is labeled separately. 2019 has no MACS2 AUPRC (absent, not invented).

pval/coverage_95.estimator_notes: α = 0.025, lo = Φ⁻¹(α; μ, σ), hi = Φ⁻¹(1 − α; μ, σ), coverage = mean(lo ≤ y ≤ hi). σ ← max(σ, 10⁻¹²). Nominal 0.95. This is interval coverage, not ECE. Computed from distributional.py::coverage_gauss, emitted in gauss_suite.
pval/coverage_95.question: What fraction of observed bins fall inside the forecast’s central 95% interval?
pval/coverage_95.read_rules: No direction; companion, never ranked. Distance from 0.95 is not a sort key. Quote with CRPS + PIT KS. Rival wrap ~0.98 is known miscalibration. On rivals this scores the wrap, not a native forecast.

pval/crps.estimator_notes: Per bin, Gneiting–Raftery 2007 closed form (distributional.py::gauss_crps): z = (y − μ) / σ with σ ← max(σ, 10⁻¹²). Track score = mean over bins; board = unweighted mean over tracks. No oracle-scaled split on this arm. Closed form only — no sampled Gaussian CRPS in this code. Rivals: σ is one constant per assay from the fitted table, not per-bin. CANDI store path: μ, σ are the delta-method pushforward of the training-space Gaussian when signal_target_transform ≠ none (invert_signal_prediction). Computed from distributional.py::gauss_crps / gauss_suite.
pval/crps.question: If each bin is a Gaussian forecast in −log10 p, how far is that whole distribution from the observed value — not just the centre?
pval/crps.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked but ordering-only. Always show PIT KS and Coverage 95 beside it. No single noise floor (t57 per-method paired CIs; ties not greyed yet). Rival wrap CRPS is in-sample for σ on chromosome 21. Never quote as a calibrated absolute. Point-only rivals get one Gaussian spread per assay, fitted once on validation-pair residuals (eval chromosome chr21) and reused unchanged. That device is known-miscalibrated (PIT KS 0.367–0.391, 95% coverage 0.977–0.985 on the stamped rival rows). CANDI's per-bin Gaussian signal head does not use this device. Count and p-value CRPS never share a column.

pval/gaussian_nll.estimator_notes: full=True Gaussian NLL (distributional.py::gaussian_nll): (1/N) Σ ½(log v_i + (μ_i − y_i)² / v_i + log(2π)), v_i = max(σ_i², 10⁻⁶). Truth is bent forward with transform_signal_target; prediction is not inverted (harness.py::loss_block). External stamped rows: transform none. Future CANDI store path: typically arcsinh — not comparable (D30). Computed from distributional.py::gaussian_nll.
pval/gaussian_nll.question: What mean per-bin Gaussian negative log-likelihood does the p-value head (or wrapped Gaussian) assign to held-out truth in the training transform?
pval/gaussian_nll.read_rules: Lower is better; per_family, never in the composite. Quote with signal_target_transform or not at all. Needs a spread (knn1 / avg-arcsinh absent). Not comparable to NB NLL. Count-space NLL and p-value-space NLL never share a table.

pval/gwcorr.estimator_notes: Pearson r = np.corrcoef(y, ŷ)[0, 1] on concatenated chromosomes. A constant input returns NaN (eic.py::gwcorr). Correlation is scale-invariant (ddof cancels). Computed from eic.py::gwcorr.
pval/gwcorr.question: Do predicted and true values rise and fall together in a straight line, over the whole scored genome?
pval/gwcorr.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; no floor. A constant forecast (marginal) is absent, not zero. Store truth and challenge truth are different measurements of the same experiment — use the truth toggle, never a rescale.

pval/gwspear.estimator_notes: ρ = scipy.stats.spearmanr(y, ŷ)[0] (eic.py::gwspear). Scipy default: average ranks on ties. Concatenated chromosomes. Computed from eic.py::gwspear.
pval/gwspear.question: Do predicted and true values share the same rank order over the scored genome?
pval/gwspear.read_rules: Higher is better; ranked; no floor. Do not quote Pearson and Spearman as a pair across spaces. Same warning across truths: use the truth toggle, never a rescale.

pval/mse.estimator_notes: Mean squared error on the concatenation of scored chromosomes (eic.dict_to_arr). No ddof. No transform. Track wrap is eic.py::mse; board number is the unweighted mean over tracks (harness.py::macro_mean). 2019 uses the same letters on a different signal, with a different macro recipe (bootstrap mean within experiment; median within assay; mean over assay medians). Computed from eic.py::mse.
pval/mse.question: On average, how far is the predicted track from the truth, bin by bin, in squared units?
pval/mse.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; no floor. P-value space (pred_space: −log10 p). Challenge truth uses the same letters on a differently processed signal; the truth toggle is how you move between them. MSE scales with mark range.

pval/mse1obs.estimator_notes: N = |y|, n = int(N * 0.01), τ = np.sort(y)[-n] (so N < 100 selects the minimum and thus the whole array). Mask y_i ≥ τ (ties admit more than 1%). Then MSE on the mask. Top-1% is over the concatenation of all scored chromosomes, not per chromosome. Computed from eic.py::mse1obs and _top1_mask.
pval/mse1obs.question: On the tallest 1% of observed bins, how far is the prediction?
pval/mse1obs.read_rules: Lower is better; ranked; no floor. The chromosome set is part of the number, and so is the truth: use the truth toggle, never a rescale.

pval/peak_base_rate.estimator_notes: peak_base_rate = mean(1[y^peak]) over scored bins (binary.py::binary_suite). Board number is the unweighted mean over tracks.
pval/peak_base_rate.question: What fraction of scored bins are MACS2 peaks in the validation cell?
pval/peak_base_rate.read_rules: Companion, never ranked; no direction. About 0.01375 on chromosome 21, about 0.0169 macro genome-wide. A random ranker’s AUPRC equals this rate. Always quote AUPRC with this number.

pval/pit_ks.estimator_notes: PIT KS is the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance of the probability-integral transform from Uniform(0,1). Continuous (non-randomised) PIT u_i = Φ((y_i − μ_i) / σ_i) with σ_i ← max(σ_i, 10⁻¹²). Then PIT-KS = scipy.stats.kstest(u, "uniform").statistic — two-sided D = sup_t |F_n(t) − t|, not a p-value. Discrete PIT (calibration_pit_curve) is not used on this arm. No jitter / randomised PIT. Computed from distributional.py::gauss_suite.
pval/pit_ks.question: If the predicted Gaussians were correct, the observed values’ percentiles would be Uniform(0,1) — how far from uniform are they?
pval/pit_ks.read_rules: Lower is better; companion, never ranked. Always beside p-value CRPS. On rivals this scores the wrap (one σ per assay, fitted on chromosome-21 validation-pair residuals), not a forecast the method emitted. Store-path CANDI: calibration of the delta-method Gaussian, not the head. Known-miscalibrated wrap: PIT KS 0.367–0.391 on the stamped rival rows.
